newsitem.title: UK: National Power drops after H1 results.
newsitem.headline: National Power drops after H1 results.

text.p: Shares in National Power Plc dropped on Wednesday after the electricity generator posted a drop in first-half profits and warned of lower output for the current year.
The stock was down 9p at 444, after on November 18 closing at a four-month high of 453.5p.

Nigel Hawkins, analyst at Yamaichi, said the results were broadly in line with expectations but the company's 27 percent UK market share -- and its expected 70 terawatt hours output for the year, down 20 percent on the year before -- looked low.
He added that he beleived the year's results would depend crucially on how cold the UK winter turns out to be.

National Power said its pre-tax profit before exceptionals fell one percent to 251 million stg in the six months to September 30, compared with expectations in a range between 210 million stg and 253 million.

"With increasing competition in the UK generation market and the impact over the full year of the divestment of the 4,000 megawatts of plant, the directors expect...output for the year to be 20 percent lower than last year," National Power said.
It said it expects competitive pressure in the UK to increase though rapid growth in earnings from overseas operations would make an increasing impact.
